doc.title: Eiji Kitamura interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: American servicemen, jazz clubs and Richard Wyands
summary: Americans came to Japanese jazz clubs; Richard Wyands toured with him having never met.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That’s nice. So you never miss a gig, right? Can you think back, after World War II, there was probably a lot of American servicemen in Japan. Did they bring the music with them? Were they listening to jazz also?
Yes. Many Americans came to jazz clubs. And they enjoyed our playing jazz. And these people, an American musician came to Japan. Richard Wyands.
And he brought his trio and joined my clarinet and a tour in Japan. The very first — I didn’t know Richard Wyands, and the first time to join.
The first time you played together, you hadn’t even met.
But the music brought you together, didn’t it?
